fixed_metric: Exactly the R776 phase-zero closed shell g0, including both end rolls and both complete disks; central tensor dx^2+(1-k Z0)^2 de^2. Identical at every iteration, phase and refinement across the three independent branches.

geometry.inherited_initial_world_columns: Use the initial-world geometry from the working quadrature on each training or check grid. The canonical final field uses order 20.
geometry.world: Fixed right full physical head, R776 actual translated left head in hard and normal-swing branches; free-left has full three-channel corrections. Every defining base sits above the original analytic axial floor at every positive phase and after the strictly positive axial transformation.
geometry.physical_fields: Uniformly short, R776 spatial arc, R778 periodic n=1 or n=2, and the independent broad normal swing with a scalar chord equation. A fraction blends the true six material jets before fitting.

limits: The shape companion columns use order 20. Inherited initial-world columns take the working quadrature on training and check grids. The canonical final field is evaluated at order 20.

Nine physical coarse candidates, three independent 4/8/16 space/time refinement chains and three complete same-runner 65+7 phase-union terminal meshes/geometry indexes. No corrugation frequency is increased on a refinement chain. All use the same R776 initial metric, phase interval and material sphere.

The full three Gram coefficients, a log-area barrier, four directional normal curvatures, both actual spectral inequalities ±II <=20g, the 96 worst true Gram Frobenius losses, and changing finite ordered normal ball inequalities enter the shape field objective. Exact metric, all-time injectivity and reach remain mathematical costs after fitting. The independent terminal scans its own finite mesh and full ordered pairs.

The global axial floor retains a genuine entire-image displacement above .315 for the intended integral field at the last phase. The right physical head is fixed at every time; the independently released left head is spatially variable. Volume and a sufficient normal-ball certificate of any optimized point remain separate.

The high-frequency R778 theorem is separate. Its rigorous best theoretical strain bound trades away quantitative reach; this run uses finite low-frequency fields and true varying physical coefficients only, with the same selected frequency throughout each continuation. All numerical readouts are finite-grid values. Raw NPZ and 3 x 7 binary meshes stay on the runner.
